Comments: On November 8, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection for a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Pad. The DEP received a phone call from Inflection Energy Zac Subra on November 6, 2021 about a release of production fluid during a pressure test. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Joe Zoka. During a pressure test for the preparation of flowback of the recently drilled wells, a valve was left open. The open valve spilled about 28 gallons of brine fluid to the pad surface. The impacted area was excavated immediately. Inflection scraped about 3 inches of a 15 ft. by 10 ft. area. The impacted soil was then loaded into a covered container to be hauled to the landfill. The containment around the flowback equipment appears to be in good condition. Inflection is planning to begin flowback process on Tuesday. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), ¿78a.56(a), and SWMA 301 are noted but have been immediately corrected. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3257683.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 966786
Permit API: 129-24375
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/26/2022
Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. However, outstanding violations issued during inspection record 3400883 shall remain open since no NOV response or any of the information requested has been received from the operator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/30/2024 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Columbia Township, Bradford county. 78A64A(E)___ - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/30/2024
Violation Code: 78A64A(E)___ - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Operator failed to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more.
Violation ID: 8173905
Permit API: 015-23837
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Columbia Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/30/2024
Comments: On 01/30/2024 representatives from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) Evan Buck, Erica Lutz, and Korey Starkey conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's CRANK (03-067) O multi-well pad located in Columbia Township, Bradford County. Upon arrival to the site at 1320 hours, weather was 29F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).The site is currently undergoing the hydraulic fracturing process. Numerous temporary storage tanks are set up onsite and stationed in secondary or tertiary containment (photos #2, 3, 6, and 7). There is also an aboveground storage tank located onsite for freshwater storage. Due to active operations, a pad-wide containment system is in place and contained standing water which field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~2.0 to 11.5 mS/cm.There are 4 existing wells capable of producing and 6 wells being hydraulically fractured located onsite (photos #4 and 5). 10 inactive gas production units (GPUs) and 2 produced fluid tanks are stationed in secondary containment are also located onsite (photo #8).Vegetative coverage surrounding the pad could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 2 infiltration basins serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photo #9).The pad contained standing water field measured for EC at a range of ~943 to 2600 us/cm. On 01/10/2024 the DEP conducted an incident response inspection (ID# 3671306) which detailed an oral and written recommendation to maintain and repair damaged containment structure near the brine offloading area. Repsol's records indicate acknowledgement of the damaged containment structure on 01/10/2024 (photo #15). During today's inspection, we noted that the same containment structure was overflowing, damaged, and discharging water onto the pad surface that field measured for EC at ~5.0 mS/cm (photos #2, 12, and 13). This discharge drained into a larger puddle which field measured for EC at ~2.60 mS/cm with a sheen visible on the surface (photos #10, 11, and 14). We collected a sample from this puddle (Sample ID# 9570-001) to be analyzed for standard analysis code 942 (photo #11).Based on the observed fluids escaping secondary containment show in photos #10-14, the DEP is citing violations against 25 PA 78a.64a(e) for failure to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more and for failure to repair the containment structure as soon as possible. The DEP may cite additional violations pending results of sample ID# 9570-001.The DEP recommends the following:-Recovering and properly disposing of all water held in containment structures onsite.-Continuing containment inspections on at least a weekly basis to prevent accidental releases.-Further monitoring, repair, and maintenance of the brine offload area and associated containment.-Screening pad material when containment structures are removed upon completion of active operations.-Maintaining the pad surface to prevent pad material and contaminated water from leaving the site.We departed the site at 1430 hours.

There is also an aboveground storage tank located onsite for freshwater storage. Due to active operations, a pad-wide containment system is in place and contained standing water which field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~2.0 to 11.5 mS/cm.There are 4 existing wells capable of producing and 6 wells being hydraulically fractured located onsite (photos #4 and 5). 10 inactive gas production units (GPUs) and 2 produced fluid tanks are stationed in secondary containment are also located onsite (photo #8).Vegetative coverage surrounding the pad could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 2 infiltration basins serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photo #9).The pad contained standing water field measured for EC at a range of ~943 to 2600 us/cm. On 01/10/2024 the DEP conducted an incident response inspection (ID# 3671306) which detailed an oral and written recommendation to maintain and repair damaged containment structure near the brine offloading area. Repsol's records indicate acknowledgement of the damaged containment structure on 01/10/2024 (photo #15). During today's inspection, we noted that the same containment structure was overflowing, damaged, and discharging water onto the pad surface that field measured for EC at ~5.0 mS/cm (photos #2, 12, and 13). This discharge drained into a larger puddle which field measured for EC at ~2.60 mS/cm with a sheen visible on the surface (photos #10, 11, and 14). We collected a sample from this puddle (Sample ID# 9570-001) to be analyzed for standard analysis code 942 (photo #11).Based on the observed fluids escaping secondary containment show in photos #10-14, the DEP is citing violations against 25 PA 78a.64a(e) for failure to remove stormwater as soon as possible and prior to the capacity of secondary containment being reduced by 10% or more and for failure to repair the containment structure as soon as possible. The DEP may cite additional violations pending results of sample ID# 9570-001.The DEP recommends the following:-Recovering and properly disposing of all water held in containment structures onsite.-Continuing containment inspections on at least a weekly basis to prevent accidental releases.-Further monitoring, repair, and maintenance of the brine offload area and associated containment.-Screening pad material when containment structures are removed upon completion of active operations.-Maintaining the pad surface to prevent pad material and contaminated water from leaving the site.We departed the site at 1430 hours.

Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8248045
Permit API: 123-47821
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/05/2025
Comments: The Loomis B Lease Loomis 7 OG well is the closest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the Loomis B lease. At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the Loomis 7 OG well. The Loomis B tank battery consists of two stock tanks, a produced fluids separator, and one subsurface produced fluids tank located inside earthen containment diking. The conventional wells on this lease were being produced at the time of this inspection. After arriving on the lease I began to inspect the condition of the tank battery. I found that the produced fluids separator and stock tanks in containment were equipped with PVC drain lines to separate any produced fluids that enter the tank battery from either the separator or the stock tanks into the subsurface produced fluids tank. At the time of this inspection, only the PVC drain line connected to the separator was found to be draining produced fluids. At the time of this inspection, the flowing PVC drain line was improperly positioned, as it was straddled on the edge of a cutout hole on the top of the subsurface produced fluids tank. The manner in which the drain line was situated allows the majority of the fluids flowing through the line to be released onto the top of the tank and ultimately onto the floor of the containment area, as opposed to inside the subsurface tank.The specific conductance of the accumulated fluid inside of the containment area measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. The soils below the fluid accumulating in the containment area also measured in excess of 20,000 microSiemens per centimeter. A visual inspection of the containment area revealed additional signs of staining and stressed/dead vegetation around the produced fluids tank similar to that resulting from the ongoing release. This evidence is an indication of previous releases inside of the containment area prior to this inspection. At the time of this inspection, it did not appear that the pooling of fluids around the subsurface produced fluids tank were accumulating at a rate consistent with the volume of fluids being released into containment by the PVC drain. This and the evidence of stressed vegetation/oil staining around the proximity of the subsurface produced fluids tank referenced above suggests that the released fluids inside of the containment area are migrating into the soil below. A conservative estimate of a one gallon per minute discharge rate over the greater than 90 minute duration that I was present to observe the release suggests that more than 90 gallons (>2bbl) were released into the containment during this inspection.Sample number 4568-004 was collected from the fluid actively flowing from the PVC drain line and sample number 4568-005 was collected from the accumulated fluids inside of the containment area adjacent the subsurface produced fluids tank. These samples were sent to the DEP lab for SAC 942 analyses. After concluding my inspection, I called Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) at 14:59 and requested that he meet me immediately on the lease. Upon his arrival, I informed Kyle that I discovered a problem with the tank battery. I gestured to the ongoing release of fluids from the improperly placed PVC drain line. Kyle immediately placed the drain line into the cutout in the subsurface produced fluids tank. Kyle then phoned another TMP official to inform them of the release, but indicated that neither he or the other TMP official seemed to be aware of who had pumped the wells on this lease today. I informed Kyle that the release of fluids would be documented in this inspection report and that a Notice of Violations (NOV) would be included.A NOV is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/14/2020
Comments: On December 14, 2020, DEP representative Brad Kline followed up on a report of a brine water spill (CTS No. 353993) that occurred on December 12, 2020. A hose containing brine from a water truck did not pump completely empty and when the hose was moved the remaining brine water spilled near the MASS outside of containment. The Department met with Beech Resources representative Don Stevenson onsite and he showed the Department where the spill occurred. The spill was estimated at 30 gallons of brine water from the hose. The area was excavated the same day as the spill occurred. Contaminated soil has been loaded into a rolloff dumpster. Beech Resources was in the process of stimulating 2 of the 4 new wells drilled on the pad. Fracking rig containment looked to be in good condition. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum the secondary containment as necessary to keep from overtopping the containment berms.The violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301 have been immediately corrected.

Report Details

Permit API: 039-25765
Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: North Shenango Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/27/2022
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint ID #366445 that is dated 8/22/2022.The complainant indicated to the Department that they had concerns regarding the installation of a stormwater discharge pipe at the site. It was stated that the stormwater basin recently overtopped and flooded the adjacent township roadway. Based upon the information from the complainant the operator installed a new discharge pipe that outlets to the roadside ditch of the township road. The ditch flows into UNT to Bennett Run (WWF).Based upon my investigation and site inspection the Department finds the following: -It appears that the sediment basins did overflow and discharge stormwater into the woods and out onto the township road.Recent activity indicates:-The two sediment basins have been cleaned out of sediment.-An earth berm along the wood line has been established between the two basins.-A graded channel/swale has been created between the basins. The southern basin flows through the swale to the northern basin.-There are several rock filters within the swale/channel.-It appears that a 4" PVC pipe has been installed from the northern basin and day lights to the roadside ditch of the township road. (Currently flowing water)The recent activity at the site regarding the post construction stormwater management of the site was not approved by the Department. The activity was not part of the original permit and therefore the operator is in violation.The site has mot been restored per state requirements for restoration and therefore is still in violation for site restoration.The well is properly labeled and there is a Site ID posting at the entrance of the site. The well appears to be shut-in and not plumbed to produce. There is a vertical separator and a 210bbl steel tank onsite in separate lined containment structures. The containment should be monitored for stormwater removal to allow for appropriate capacity of the containment. There are also several other pieces of equipment onsite including: a natural gas-powered electric generator skid and several steel structures for bitcoin computer generation. A contractor onsite during the inspection indicated that the equipment was being dismantled and removed from the site.The operator has reported "no" production for the well from January 2022 through July 2022. Seven consecutive months reported with no production. The Department requests information regarding the intentions of the operator to produce the well within the the next 3 months. A well is required to produce within a 12 month period to maintain "Active" status. Otherwise, the well is considered to be abandoned. Outstanding / New violations are cited.

Permit API: 125-27410
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024, routine inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources Inc well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on April 1, 2016.The following was observed:Well 10H was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 1 and 2). A small amount of grease was observed on the well pad surface below the well head (see photo 3). There are five other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production. The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 4). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 5). Additional secondary containment that appeared to be severely deteriorated was observed next to the production tanks (see photo 6). This appears to be used for pump trucks that empty the production tanks. The ERP and PPC plan were onsite (see photos 7 and 8). Deep accelerated erosion rills were observed in multiple portions of the access road, with one of them appearing to empty into a storm culvert (see photos 11-15). The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that any grease or other fluids used during routine maintenance that fall onto the well pad surface are immediately removed. The Department also recommends that deteriorated secondary containments and other onsite equipment are replaced to mitigate the risk of a spill from occurring on site. Finally, the Department recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that contain regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severely eroded access road.

Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Robinson 13 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Fayette County following the receipt of a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) on 1/28/26.A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/3/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 1/3/2026 and a well site restoration report be submitted to the Department by 3/4/2026. IR 4153788 documents the return of the WSRR.At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe a Post-Plugging Site Restoration Plan on along the shared access road, the direct access road or the plugged well site. Violations were issued during IR 4153788 for failure to have a post-plugging site restoration plan on site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the direct portion of the access road that leads to the plugged well site to be a partially vegetated dirt road with muddy tire tracks throughout. These tire tracks continue onto the plugged well site. At the time of this inspection, the plugged well site appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth everywhere except where the tire tracks were observed. Compost Filter Sock appeared to be spread along the perimeters of the plugged well site. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate GPS location of the plugged well. No equipment associated with the plugging of the well or the plugged well site was observed at this time. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued to this plugged gas well for failure to comply with a COA of the Department due to the access road and plugged well site being unrestored.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/28/2022 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/28/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 980782
Permit API: 015-22203
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/28/2022
Comments: On 12/28/2022, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Maggie well site. It was 42 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Due to snow cover, site stabilization could not be adequately assessed during the inspection. PCSM is addressed by five retentive grading/infiltration areas that appeared to be functioning as designed.There were five wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Two of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment.There was Halliburton equipment stored on site for fracking operations at a nearby facility. There were two equipment and three tank trailers in the northwest corner of the pad. I field tested water puddles in the melting ice in a 50' x 50' area around the trailers for conductivity with an Oakton PCTS 50 with results as follows:8.61 mS conductance in ice/water puddle under a tank trailer labeled as LD-28009.16 mS conductance underneath a tank trailer placarded as 3265 Corrosive. Water/ice puddles near scraped pile of snow at the edge of the pad field tested at 11.04 mS conductance.10' x 20' water puddle under front of hard pipe trailer field tested at >20.0 mS conductance.During the inspection and sample collection, the ice melted considerably, forming separate water/ice puddles. One long puddle formed that was approximately 3' wide at the east end and 20' wide on the west end, and being 40' long and 0.5" deep. This puddle stretched across the areas sampled with elevated conductance. I sampled other melting areas north of this puddle with results less than 1.0 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-038 for laboratory analysis from the area with the >20.0 mS conductance reading.Halliburton personnel were on site and were in the process of moving the trailers to the Chesapeake Floydie well pad. One of the Halliburton employees informed me that the tank trailers were empty of fluids. I did witness a white residue on the frames of all five trailers.I contacted Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein who said that he would mobilize someone to the site to assess the area described with elevated conductance. He is also going to discuss with Halliburton possible causes of the elevated conductance readings. Chesapeake's Tim Long showed up before I finished the inspection and I did show him where I got the elevated readings from. He said that Joe Button was mobilizing a vac truck to location to remove the liquid from the identified areas.Because of the elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.I left the site at 1500 hours.

Inspection Date 2016-12-19
Comments This administrative inspection has been created to document a production fill spill in the range of (10-20) gallons to the pad surface that occurred on 12-8-16 as documented in the Department's 12-9-16 inspection report. Cabot submitted a Remediation Summary Report prepared by Resource Environmental of Montrose, PA to the Department on 12-15-16. The report contains a site map of the release area and perimeter of excavation, (5) test pit locations dug for soil conductivity screening, conductivity readings measured after the final excavation and a remediation summary report containing a description of the incident, remedial action and waste disposal information. The description of the incident in the report states that the following. The spill of (10-20) gallons occurred on 12-8-16. An unanticipated surge of production fluid flowed through the dump line to the production fluid tanks when a well tender was performing maintenance. The spill impacted the immediate area of the production fluid tanks. The remedial action in the report states the following. Cabot had disassembled and relocated the dump lines and production fluid tanks on 12/9/16 to provide access to the immediate area. GasSearch Drilling Services performed the excavation of the impacted area under the direction of Resource. Resource characterized impacted soil by visual observations and field screening the soils for electrical conductivity. The highest soil conductivity measured by Resource in impacted area with dark staining was (568) micro Siemens/cm³. Where light staining of the impacted area was observed, the soil conductivity readings were less than (60) µs/cm³. Post excavation soil conductivity readings were less than or equal to (59) µs/cm³. The dimensions of the excavation were 50' x 42'. The typical excavation depth was 1 to 3 inches, but was measured at (10) inches where dark staining was observed. Approximately eighteen (18) cubic yards of impacted soils were loaded directly into two (2), lined, 30 cubic yard, roll-off containers for off-site disposal at an approved facility. Cabot has concluded that characterization and post remediation field screenings demonstrate that no additional remediation is related to this release. The Department reviewed the report on 12/16/19 and has concluded that no further action is warranted of Cabot at this time. Violations immediately corrected are associated with the R Warriner 4H well. Please forward the waste disposal manifests to the Department upon receipt. Please feel free to contact me with any questions at 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov. The following well permits have been issued for this location: R Warriner 4H; 115-20275 R Warriner 8H; 115-20348

The report contains a site map of the release area and perimeter of excavation, (5) test pit locations dug for soil conductivity screening, conductivity readings measured after the final excavation and a remediation summary report containing a description of the incident, remedial action and waste disposal information. The description of the incident in the report states that the following. The spill of (10-20) gallons occurred on 12-8-16. An unanticipated surge of production fluid flowed through the dump line to the production fluid tanks when a well tender was performing maintenance. The spill impacted the immediate area of the production fluid tanks. The remedial action in the report states the following. Cabot had disassembled and relocated the dump lines and production fluid tanks on 12/9/16 to provide access to the immediate area. GasSearch Drilling Services performed the excavation of the impacted area under the direction of Resource. Resource characterized impacted soil by visual observations and field screening the soils for electrical conductivity. The highest soil conductivity measured by Resource in impacted area with dark staining was (568) micro Siemens/cm³. Where light staining of the impacted area was observed, the soil conductivity readings were less than (60) µs/cm³. Post excavation soil conductivity readings were less than or equal to (59) µs/cm³. The dimensions of the excavation were 50' x 42'. The typical excavation depth was 1 to 3 inches, but was measured at (10) inches where dark staining was observed. Approximately eighteen (18) cubic yards of impacted soils were loaded directly into two (2), lined, 30 cubic yard, roll-off containers for off-site disposal at an approved facility. Cabot has concluded that characterization and post remediation field screenings demonstrate that no additional remediation is related to this release. The Department reviewed the report on 12/16/19 and has concluded that no further action is warranted of Cabot at this time. Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8228362
Permit API: 015-23794
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 4/10/2025
Comments: On 04/09/2025 at 1400 hours Chesapeake Appalachia (Expand) representative Mike Deming reported a 15 gallon release at the Deremer Well Pad in Tuscarora Township, Bradford County. The DEP spoke with Mike Deming on the phone. He stated a valve in the suction knockout line cracked due to freezing temperatures. Based on weather conditions the release began at approximately 0930 hours. The release was discovered by a representative at approximately 1100 hours. The area was marked and a truck will be onsite to recover the water. Water from the release was reported to be field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~ 1.8 mS/cm. Creston Environmental will be onsite to collect samples. On 04/10/2025 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report at the Deremer Well Pad. The DEP met representative Mike Deming and a Creston Environmental team onsite. The weather was 34 degrees and cloudy. I arrived at 0910 hours. The material and water has been properly recovered in area of the release (photo #2-4). The cracked valve was replaced on the same day as the release (photo #5). Creston Environmental conducted sampling of the area. There was no pooled water remaining in the area of the release. A crew completed cleanup of the release on the same day (04/09/2025). The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There were several infiltration berms onsite. They appeared to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 267-843 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional releases or spills. There was one produced fluid tank equipped with an internal secondary containment. There were seven gas processing units (GPUs) onsite. There were seven wells capable of producing onsite. They were properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. Based on the reported release the following violations are cited as immediately corrected against API# 015-23794:CLS 402(b) I departed at 1050 hours.

Comments: On 1/22/2019 at approximately 1100, I conducted an incident response inspection of the Cosgray well site located in Franklin Township, Greene County in response to a reported spill of produced water. On 1/21/2019 at 1400, a valve leak as a mist was noticed by the operator. The operator approximated that less than 40 gallons of produced water released from a GPU as a result. Specialized Professional Services (SPSI) responded to remediate the impacted area. During the 1/22/2019 inspection, the following was observed: * Act 9 sign located at the site entrance was in good condition. * Some secondary containment mechanisms utilized on 4 GPUs but containment appeared unable to hold 110% of the unit storage capacity. * SPSI was on site during the inspection cleaning the GPUs. * Liquid observed in the grated tray between the GPUs. * Well identification tags were not able to be found on any wells. An oil sheen was observed in one well cellar (37-125-27404). * Production fluid tanks were within secondary containment and appeared in good condition. Violations were identified during this inspection and will be assessed to each individual well.
